entry.title: From a Custom SAP Table to an SAP Fiori Analytical Application: An End-to-End Guide
entry.content:
Introduction

One of the most common requirements in SAP S/4HANA projects is to make SAP table data available to business users through SAP Fiori applications.

When addressing this requirement, organizations often consider developing a custom SAPUI5 application, creating a custom transaction or classical ABAP report, building an SAP GUI–based query such as SQVI or SQ01, or providing direct table access. However, direct access to database tables is generally not suitable for business users because it exposes technical structures, may introduce authorization risks, and does not provide a business-oriented user experience.

For many analytical reporting scenarios, SAP S/4HANA provides standard extensibility capabilities that can significantly reduce development effort. This guide demonstrates an end-to-end approach for exposing data from a custom SAP table through an SAP Fiori analytical application using an ABAP CDS view, the Custom CDS Views app, the Custom Analytical Queries app, and SAP Fiori launchpad configuration.

The guide also explains how to register the key-user extensibility artifacts for transport so that they can be moved consistently across the system landscape.

The implementation shown in this article is based on an SAP S/4HANA on-premise or private cloud system. Application names, available features, and configuration steps may differ depending on the SAP S/4HANA release and deployment model.

Background and Motivation

This guide is based on a reporting requirement I encountered while working with SAP S/4HANA. The initial requirement was straightforward: make data from a custom SAP table available to business users in SAP Fiori without developing a separate SAPUI5 application or granting direct table access.

During the implementation, I evaluated different approaches and eventually used a combination of ABAP CDS, Custom CDS Views, Custom Analytical Queries, and standard SAP Fiori Launchpad configuration. Since I found that the required information was distributed across different documentation and SAP Community resources, I decided to document the complete process in one end-to-end guide.

The screenshots and implementation steps in this article are based on a solution that I implemented and tested in an SAP S/4HANA sandbox environment.

Table of Contents

  • What You Will Build
  • Solution Architecture
  • Before You Start: Choosing the Right Approach
  • Implementation Steps
  • Summary
  • Key Takeaways
  • Complete Solution Flow
  • References

What You Will Build

This guide demonstrates how to transform data from a custom SAP table into an SAP Fiori analytical application using standard SAP S/4HANA development, extensibility, and launchpad tools.

📁Source: Custom database table

↓

📊Result: Analytical report in SAP Fiori launchpad

Note: Although this guide uses a custom SAP table, the overall approach can also be applied to other CDS-based data sources. Before reusing a CDS view, verify that it is released for the intended use, supports the required modeling capabilities, and provides the appropriate analytical semantics for your reporting scenario.

Solution Architecture

The following diagram provides an overview of the complete implementation flow covered in this guide.

Before You Start: Choosing the Right Approach

Before starting the implementation, determine whether a developer-created ABAP CDS view is actually required.

First, check whether SAP already provides a released CDS view that fulfills the business requirement. Reusing SAP-delivered CDS content can reduce development effort, preserve business semantics, and simplify future upgrades.

For example, when building an analytical report for journal-entry data, a released SAP-delivered CDS view such as I_JournalEntryItem may be more appropriate than accessing the underlying ACDOCA table directly. However, the selected CDS view must still be checked for release status, supported capabilities, analytical semantics, and suitability for the intended scenario.

Creating a custom ABAP CDS view in ABAP Development Tools may be necessary when:

  • No suitable SAP-delivered CDS view is available.
  • The source data is stored in a custom database table.
  • Additional joins, transformations, or calculated fields cannot be implemented in the Custom CDS Views app.
  • The required source or association is not supported by key-user extensibility.

Because this article demonstrates a complete end-to-end implementation, it starts with a custom ABAP CDS view based on a custom database table.

💡 Tip from my implementation: Before creating a new CDS view in Eclipse, I recommend checking whether SAP already provides a released standard CDS view for the required data. This can considerably simplify the implementation.

Implementation Steps

The following sections demonstrate the complete implementation process step by step.

Step 1 – Create the ABAP CDS View

The first step is to create an ABAP CDS view based on the custom database table. This view will serve as the developer-created data source that is later consumed by SAP S/4HANA key-user extensibility applications.

1.1 Create a New ABAP CDS View

In Eclipse with ABAP Development Tools (ADT), right-click the relevant package and choose New → Other ABAP Repository Object.

Select Data Definition from the available repository object types and continue with the creation wizard.

Enter a name and description for the data definition, select the appropriate package, and choose Next.

Assign the object to a transport request. If the object is created as a local object for testing purposes, select $TMP; otherwise, use a transportable development package.

After assigning the transport request, select the appropriate CDS template and choose Finish to create the data definition.

1.2 Define the CDS View

Define the ABAP CDS view using the custom database table as its data source. The example is intentionally kept simple because the primary purpose of this article is to demonstrate how the data is consumed by SAP S/4HANA analytical and launchpad applications rather than to explain ABAP CDS development in detail.

The custom table used in this example contains company code, trading partner, account-range, and activation-status fields. The selected key fields should reflect the actual uniqueness and business semantics of the source table.

Add the required fields to the CDS view and define the appropriate key fields.

To make the ABAP CDS view available as a data source for key-user CDS modeling, add the required supported-capabilities annotation:

@ObjectModel.supportedCapabilities: [
  #CDS_MODELING_DATA_SOURCE,
  #CDS_MODELING_ASSOCIATION_TARGET
]

#CDS_MODELING_DATA_SOURCE allows the view to be used as a CDS modeling data source. #CDS_MODELING_ASSOCIATION_TARGET allows it to be used as an association target where supported.

Note: The CDS view in this example is intentionally simple. Production implementations may require associations, calculated fields, semantic annotations, authorization controls, and additional data-modeling logic.

The resulting CDS implementation is shown below:

@AbapCatalog.sqlViewName: 'ZDDL_C_TPACC'
@AccessControl.authorizationCheck: #NOT_REQUIRED
@Metadata.allowExtensions: true
@EndUserText.label: 'CDS View for Trading Partner Account Mapping'
@ObjectModel.usageType: {
    serviceQuality: #A,
    sizeCategory: #S,
    dataClass: #CUSTOMIZING
}
@ObjectModel.supportedCapabilities: [
    #CDS_MODELING_DATA_SOURCE,
    #CDS_MODELING_ASSOCIATION_TARGET
]
define view ZPS_C_TPACC
    as select from zps_t_tpartacc
{
    key bukrs,
    key vbund,
    key kstarfrm,
    key kstarokg8,
        kstarto,
        kstarlid,
        active
}

Important: The annotation @AccessControl.authorizationCheck: #NOT_REQUIRED is used only for this simplified demonstration. In a productive implementation, define and test an appropriate authorization concept based on the sensitivity of the exposed data.

Activate the CDS view after completing the implementation.

1.3 Release the CDS View for Use in Key-User Applications

Before the ABAP CDS view can be selected in key-user extensibility applications, it must be released for the appropriate use.

Open the API State settings for the CDS view in ADT and release it under the Use in Key User Apps (C1) contract. This release contract makes the view available to supported key-user extensibility applications such as Custom CDS Views.

The exact menu and available release contracts may differ depending on the SAP S/4HANA and ADT versions used in your system.

Important: In my test, creating and activating the ABAP CDS view was not sufficient to make it visible in the Custom CDS Views app. The view became selectable only after I maintained the supported capabilities and released it under the C1 contract. This was one of the main reasons I included the release step explicitly in this guide.

Spoiler
SAP S/4HANA 2025 Simplification

Newer SAP S/4HANA and ABAP development environments may provide additional options for generating an SAP Fiori elements application from a service binding.

In this alternative approach, the CDS model is exposed through a service definition and service binding. 


The service can then be previewed and, depending on the available development tools and system release, used to generate an SAP Fiori elements application.


This alternative is different from the key-user analytical-query approach demonstrated in the remainder of this article. Its availability and exact workflow depend on the SAP S/4HANA edition, release, feature package, and installed ADT version.

For more information, see:
Creating SAP Fiori App from Service Binding | SAP Help Portal
Quickly Generate and Deploy SAP Fiori Apps from AB... - SAP Community

Step 2 – Create the Custom CDS View

The released ABAP CDS view can now be used as the primary data source in the Custom CDS Views app. In this step, you will create a custom CDS view using the Cube scenario to prepare the data for analytical reporting.

Open the Custom CDS Views app from the SAP Fiori launchpad.

Choose Create to create a new Custom CDS View. Enter the required header information and select Cube as the scenario.

Note: The Cube scenario is selected because the resulting data model will be consumed by a custom analytical query. Other Custom CDS View scenarios serve different consumption purposes and are not covered in this guide.

Select the previously released ABAP CDS view as the primary data source.

If required, define additional calculated fields, associations, filters, or semantic settings.

Note: Since my source table contained mapping and status information rather than business amounts or quantities, it did not provide a natural numeric measure. However, the Cube scenario still required at least one measure. I therefore added a Record Count measure and kept it hidden because it was needed by the analytical model but was not relevant to the report users.

Add the Record Count measure and set its visibility to Hidden.

Review the field properties and analytical settings. When the configuration is complete, save and publish the custom CDS view.

Step 3 – Create a Custom Analytical Query

After publishing the custom CDS view, create a custom analytical query that defines how the data will be presented to business users. The query allows you to configure dimensions, measures, filters, sorting, display properties, and other analytical settings.

Open the Custom Analytical Queries app from the SAP Fiori launchpad.

Choose Create to create a new analytical query.

Enter the required header information and select the previously published Custom CDS View as the data source.

Select the required fields and define how they should be displayed in the report.

After configuring the fields and query properties, save the query as a draft. Publish it when the configuration is ready for testing.

Use Preview to confirm that the query returns the expected records, dimensions, measures, and filter behavior.

Important: Validate the query result before continuing with the SAP Fiori launchpad configuration. Correct any missing fields, aggregation issues, authorization problems, or unexpected analytical behavior at this stage.

Open the Query Information section and record the technical query name shown in the SQL View Name field. This value will be used as the BSA_QUERY parameter when configuring the launchpad application.

Step 4 – Create an SAP Fiori Application

4.1 Create a Semantic Object

Before configuring the launchpad application, create a semantic object for intent-based navigation.

For a customer-created semantic object, open transaction /UI2/SEMOBJ. Enter a meaningful technical name and description that represent the business purpose of the analytical application. Customer-specific semantic objects should follow the naming conventions defined by your organization.

Note: The SAP Community article referenced in this guide demonstrates the creation of a semantic object using transaction /UI2/SEMOBJ_SAP. However, SAP distinguishes between /UI2/SEMOBJ_SAP, which is intended for SAP-delivered semantic objects, and /UI2/SEMOBJ, which is intended for customer-created semantic objects. Therefore, /UI2/SEMOBJ is recommended for a custom implementation.

The screenshot below was captured from an implementation that used /UI2/SEMOBJ. 

The semantic object will be combined with an action in the SAP Fiori Launchpad App Manager to create the navigation intent for the application.

4.2 Configure the SAP Fiori Application

Open the SAP Fiori Launchpad App Manager using transaction /UI2/FLPAM. Create or open the technical catalog that will contain the launchpad app descriptor.

Choose Add App and select Web Dynpro Application as the application type.

Maintain the application title, subtitle if required, semantic object, action, and icon. Use the same semantic object created in the previous step and define an action that clearly describes the application intent, such as display or analyze.

Configure the target mapping for the generic analytical Web Dynpro application used in your system. Maintain the technical name recorded in the Query Information section as the value of the BSA_QUERY parameter. This parameter identifies the analytical query that will be opened when the user launches the application.

If the query should be executed immediately when the application is opened, maintain the BSA_EXECUTE parameter with the value X, where supported by your system configuration.

Parameter NameDefault Value
bsa_query 2CXXX_XXXXXXXX
sap-ui-tech-hint WDA
sap-ushell-next-navmode explace
sap-keep-alive true
sap-tag superiorAction

Under the Tiles tab, define the title, subtitle, and icon that will be displayed in the SAP Fiori Launchpad. 

Save the launchpad app descriptor when the configuration is complete.

Step 5 – Assign the Application to a Business Role

To make the application available to end users, the launchpad content must be provided through a business catalog and assigned to an appropriate business role.

A technical catalog contains the original launchpad app descriptor and target mapping. A business catalog references the relevant launchpad content and is assigned to the business roles used by end users.

Open the Maintain Business Roles app and select the business role that should provide access to the analytical application.

Add the business catalog that references the launchpad content created in the technical catalog.

Save and publish the business role.

To make the application visible in a specific launchpad layout, add it to an appropriate page, assign the page to a space, and assign that space to the business role.

Note: Catalog assignment controls application access, while spaces and pages control how the application is organized and presented in the SAP Fiori launchpad.

Step 6 – Launch and Validate the Application

After assigning and publishing the business role, sign in to the SAP Fiori launchpad with a user who has the required role.

The new analytical application should be available in the assigned space and page. Depending on the system and session state, the user may need to sign out and sign in again before newly assigned launchpad content becomes visible.

Open the application and verify that the analytical query loads successfully.

The data from the custom SAP table is now available to authorized business users through an SAP Fiori analytical application without the need to develop a custom SAPUI5 application.

Validate the displayed data, filters, aggregations, navigation behavior, and user authorizations before releasing the application for productive use.

In the sandbox test, I validated the application with a user assigned to the target business role rather than only with my implementation user. This helped confirm both the launchpad visibility and the authorization behavior from the end-user perspective.

Step 7 – Register the Key-User Extensions for Transport

The custom CDS view and custom analytical query created with key-user extensibility tools must be registered for transport before they can be moved to another system.

Open the Configure Software Packages app and choose Register Extensions for Transport.

Select the custom CDS view, custom analytical query, and any related key-user extensibility artifacts. Assign them to the appropriate software package and transport request.

Release and import the transport according to your organization’s transport-management process.

Important: Register Extensions for Transport covers the key-user extensibility artifacts. The developer-created ABAP CDS view, semantic object, launchpad content, business catalogs, business roles, spaces, and pages may require separate transport or content-management procedures. Verify that every artifact in the solution has been assigned to the appropriate transport mechanism.

Summary

This guide demonstrated how to expose data from a custom SAP table through an SAP Fiori analytical application using standard SAP S/4HANA development, extensibility, analytics, and launchpad tools.

The implementation started with a developer-created ABAP CDS view and continued with a custom CDS view using the Cube scenario. A custom analytical query was then created to define the report structure and analytical behavior. Finally, the query was made available through SAP Fiori launchpad content and assigned to a business role.

This approach can reduce the need for custom SAPUI5 development in analytical reporting scenarios while providing an application that is integrated with SAP Fiori launchpad navigation, roles, and transport processes.

The exact implementation and transport steps may vary depending on the SAP S/4HANA edition, system release, deployment model, and extensibility strategy.

One of the main lessons from this implementation was that a separate custom SAPUI5 application was not necessary for this reporting requirement. The most important design decisions were selecting the correct released data source, making the developer-created CDS view available to key-user extensibility, and planning the transport of the different artifact types separately. Combining these tools allowed me to keep the solution close to SAP standard while still meeting the reporting requirement.

Key Takeaways

  • Check for a suitable released SAP-delivered CDS view before creating a custom data source.
  • Use the Custom CDS Views app when the required analytical data model can be implemented with supported key-user extensibility capabilities.
  • Create an ABAP CDS view in ADT when the source data or modeling requirements cannot be handled appropriately by the Custom CDS Views app.
  • Validate the analytical query before creating the launchpad application.
  • Use customer-specific semantic objects and maintain a consistent intent-based navigation design.
  • Plan the transport of developer extensibility, key-user extensibility, launchpad content, and authorization artifacts separately.
  • Test the complete application with the authorizations of a representative business user.

Complete Solution Flow

  1. Custom database table
  2. Developer-created ABAP CDS view in ADT
  3. C1 release for use in key-user applications
  4. Custom CDS view using the Cube scenario
  5. Custom analytical query
  6. Customer-created semantic object
  7. Launchpad app descriptor and target mapping
  8. Business catalog
  9. Business role
  10. Space and page assignment
  11. SAP Fiori launchpad validation
  12. Transport of the relevant artifacts

References

entry.title: Adding Fields to Standard SAP Fiori Analytical Reports Beyond Key-User Extensibility
entry.content:
Introduction

SAP S/4HANA provides many standard analytical applications that already cover a wide range of reporting requirements. However, sooner or later, a familiar question arises:

Can an additional field be added to a standard SAP Fiori analytical report?

As an SAP CO/PS consultant, I was accustomed to working with classical reporting tools such as S_ALR_87013611, CJI3, and Report Painter/Writer. These tools remain useful, but their reporting scope is generally determined by the fields and structures provided by the standard report.

While working with CDS-based SAP Fiori analytical applications such as Projects – Actuals and Cost Centers – Actuals, I started exploring how these applications can be enhanced when additional reporting information is required.

SAP provides key-user extensibility options through the Custom Fields and Logic app, including Custom Fields, Data Source Extensions, and Custom Logic. These supported options should be evaluated first.

But what happens if the required field is not available through these options, or if its value must be derived from another data source?

This does not necessarily mean that a separate custom report must be created. If the analytical application is based on an extensible CDS model, it may be possible to enhance the underlying analytical Cube and Query using ABAP Development Tools (ADT).

I encountered this requirement in the standard Projects – Actuals application. A Supplier field was available in the journal entry data, but it was not populated for every relevant posting scenario. The reporting requirement was therefore to use the journal entry Supplier when available and otherwise derive the Supplier from the related Purchase Order.

This article explains how I implemented that requirement by extending I_JournalEntryItemCube and C_ProjectQ2201, while allowing users to continue working with the original standard SAP Fiori application.

Table of Contents

  • Choosing the Right Extension Approach
  • The Example: Adding a Reporting Supplier to Projects – Actuals
  • Finding the CDS Model Behind the Fiori Report
  • Checking Whether the CDS Can Be Extended
  • Creating the Cube Extension in ADT
  • Extending the Analytical Query
  • Verifying the Result in Projects – Actuals
  • Things to Consider
  • Key Takeaways
  • Conclusion
  • References

Choosing the Right Extension Approach

Before creating a CDS Extension in ADT, it is important to check whether development is actually necessary.

If the required field can be made available through a Data Source Extension in the Custom Fields and Logic app, this is usually the simpler and more upgrade-stable approach.

However, developer extensibility can become relevant when:

  • the required information is not available through the provided extensibility fields,
  • information needs to be retrieved from another CDS View,
  • an additional association is required, or
  • a new reporting characteristic requires additional derivation logic in the CDS layer.

For this reason, I would approach an additional-field requirement in a standard analytical application in the following order:

The available options depend on the application, business context, and SAP release. The purpose of this decision path is to prioritize supported key-user extensibility before introducing a developer extension in ADT.

The main idea is to start with the supported key-user extensibility options before moving to developer extensibility. If the requirement can be covered by a Data Source Extension or suitable Custom Logic, there is no need to introduce additional ADT development.

If these options are not sufficient, the next step is to identify the CDS model behind the analytical application and check whether the relevant CDS views can be extended.

💡Tip: For reporting requirements, I would first check Data Source Extensions before considering a CDS extension in ADT. Creating a new Custom Field is a different scenario and is mainly relevant when new business information needs to be introduced and persisted in the supported business context.

The Example: Adding a Reporting Supplier to Projects – Actuals

For the practical example in this article, I will use the standard SAP Fiori analytical application Projects – Actuals.

The requirement was to provide a Supplier characteristic for project actual costs. A standard Supplier field could already be exposed through the available Data Source Extension. However, this field reflected the Supplier stored in the journal entry and was empty in some of the relevant posting scenarios.

The requirement was therefore not simply to expose another existing field. A new Reporting Supplier characteristic was needed with the following derivation logic:

  • If a Supplier is available on the journal entry, use this Supplier.
  • If the journal entry Supplier is empty and a Purchasing Document is available, determine the Supplier from the related Purchase Order.
  • Present the derived value as a single Reporting Supplier characteristic in Projects – Actuals.

This required an additional association to the Purchase Order data source and derivation logic in the CDS layer.

Note: The screenshots and example data shown in this blog were created in a sandbox system and do not represent productive business data.

Finding the CDS Model Behind the Fiori Report

Once it was clear that the requirement could not be covered by the available key-user extensibility options, the next challenge was to identify the CDS objects behind the standard Fiori report.

For a functional consultant, this is an important step because the name of the Fiori application does not necessarily tell us which analytical Query or Cube is providing the data.

For Projects – Actuals, the relevant analytical Query is: C_ProjectQ2201

Opening the Query in ADT shows that it consumes: I_JournalEntryItemCube

This gives us the relevant analytical stack for the extension: Projects – Actuals → C_ProjectQ2201 → I_JournalEntryItemCube

First, identify the technical query name from the Fiori application.

In the system used for this example, the generated analytical query name is 2CCFIPROJECTQ2201. Open transaction RSRT, enter this technical query name, and display the query information.

In the query’s technical information, the DDL Source Name identifies the CDS analytical query.

Choose Technical Information to display the generated query details. In this example, the DDL Source Name identifies the underlying CDS analytical query as C_ProjectQ2201.

Once the DDL Source Name is known, open C_ProjectQ2201 in ABAP Development Tools (ADT). You can use Open ABAP Development Object (Ctrl + Shift + A) and search for C_ProjectQ2201. Inspecting the CDS definition shows that the Query consumes I_JournalEntryItemCube as its analytical data source.

We have now identified the relevant analytical stack: 

Projects – Actuals → 2CCFIPROJECTQ2201 → C_ProjectQ2201 → I_JournalEntryItemCube

This distinction is important for the implementation. The additional reporting logic will be introduced at the Cube level, while the Query extension will expose the resulting characteristic to the standard analytical report.

Checking Whether the CDS Can Be Extended

Before implementing the solution, the next question is whether the identified CDS objects can be extended.

In the SAP S/4HANA release used for this implementation, both I_JournalEntryItemCube and C_ProjectQ2201 are classic CDS views. Therefore, the corresponding EXTEND VIEW syntax can be used.

A practical way to validate the approach is to create a minimal CDS extension in ADT and perform a syntax and activation check before implementing the complete logic. This is exactly what I did before continuing with the solution.

💡Tip: Validate both the Cube and the analytical query. Successfully extending the Cube alone does not guarantee that the new characteristic can also be exposed through the query used by the application.

Creating the Cube Extension in ADT

After confirming that the analytical Cube can be extended, the next step is to create the CDS Extension in ABAP Development Tools.

In ADT, right-click the relevant development package and select: New → Other ABAP Repository Object.

Search for Data Definition and continue with Next.

Enter the name and description for the new Data Definition and assign the appropriate package and transport request. In this example, the Cube extension was created as: ZFI_X_JEITEMCUBE_PO.

Note: The object names shown in this blog are examples. Use the naming convention defined for your development landscape.

In the template selection, choose Extend View. I_JournalEntryItemCube is defined as a classic CDS View in this example, so the corresponding Extend View template is used.

💡Tip: If the target CDS is defined as a CDS View Entity, use the corresponding Extend View Entity template instead.

Create the CDS Extension for I_JournalEntryItemCube using the Extend View template.

The journal entry Cube already provides the PurchasingDocument field. To implement the derivation logic described earlier, I used the standard CDS view I_PurchaseOrderAPI01, which provides the PurchaseOrder key and the corresponding Supplier.

The Cube extension associates I_JournalEntryItemCube.PurchasingDocument with I_PurchaseOrderAPI01.PurchaseOrder. A CASE expression then returns the journal entry Supplier when available and otherwise uses the Supplier from the related Purchase Order. The result is exposed as a single Reporting Supplier characteristic.

The complete Cube extension is shown below.

Note: The following code reflects the CDS syntax and objects available in the system used for this implementation. Verify the availability and extensibility of the relevant CDS views in your own system before implementation.

@AbapCatalog.sqlViewAppendName: 'ZFIJEIPOEXT'
@EndUserText.label: 'JE Item Cube Extension for PO Supplier'

extend view I_JournalEntryItemCube
  with ZFI_X_JEITEMCUBE_PO

  association [0..1] to I_PurchaseOrderAPI01 as _ZPurchaseOrder
    on $projection.purchasingdocument = _ZPurchaseOrder.PurchaseOrder

{
  @EndUserText.label: 'Reporting Supplier'
  case
    when $projection.Supplier is not null
     and $projection.Supplier <> ''
      then $projection.Supplier
    else _ZPurchaseOrder.Supplier
  end as ZZ1_ReportingSupplier,

  _ZPurchaseOrder
}

Extending the Analytical Query

After activating the Cube Extension, the new characteristic becomes available at the Cube level. However, this alone does not automatically expose it in the analytical Query used by the Fiori application. The next step is therefore to extend C_ProjectQ2201 and expose the newly created characteristic to the Query.

Create another Data Definition in ADT using the Extend View template, this time for C_ProjectQ2201. In this example, the Query Extension was created as: ZFI_X_PROJECTQ2201_PO.

@AbapCatalog.sqlViewAppendName: 'ZFIPRQPOEXT'
@EndUserText.label: 'Projects Actuals Query Extension for PO Supplier'

extend view C_ProjectQ2201
  with ZFI_X_PROJECTQ2201_PO
{
  @EndUserText.label: 'Reporting Supplier'
  @AnalyticsDetails.query.axis: #FREE
  @AnalyticsDetails.query.totals: #SHOW
  I_JournalEntryItemCube.ZZ1_ReportingSupplier
    as ZZ1_ReportingSupplier
}

The Query Extension exposes the characteristic created at the Cube level and makes it available to the analytical Query.

@AnalyticsDetails.query.axis: #FREE makes the characteristic available as a free characteristic, allowing users to add it to the report when required.

Verifying the Result in Projects – Actuals

After activating both extensions, return to the standard Projects – Actuals application.

The newly added Reporting Supplier characteristic is now available in the report and can be selected like the other analytical characteristics.

Add Reporting Supplier to the report and execute the analysis.

The important point is that the original SAP Fiori application has not been copied or replaced. Users continue working with the same standard Projects – Actuals application; the additional characteristic is provided through the underlying CDS extensions.

Things to Consider

Although this approach provides a flexible way to enhance standard CDS-based analytical applications, there are a few important points to consider:

  • Not every SAP Fiori application follows the same analytical architecture. The approach described in this article applies to applications based on an extensible CDS analytical model.
  • Check key-user extensibility first. If the requirement can already be covered through Data Source Extensions or supported Custom Logic in the Custom Fields and Logic app, an additional ADT development may not be necessary.
  • Check the extensibility of the underlying CDS objects early. Both the Cube and the Query must support the required extension approach.
  • Use suitable SAP-delivered CDS data sources. When information is retrieved from another CDS view, consider whether that view is appropriate for the intended usage.
  • Consider the analytical impact of associations carefully. Cardinality and join conditions are particularly important because an incorrect relationship can lead to duplicated records, unexpected analytical results, or performance issues.
  • Test the complete analytical result. Successful activation confirms the technical implementation, but the final report should also be tested with different business scenarios to verify the derived values and aggregations.

Key Takeaways

  • Evaluate supported key-user extensibility options before introducing an ADT development.
  • Identify the complete analytical stack behind the SAP Fiori application.
  • Add new reporting logic at the Cube level and expose the resulting characteristic through the analytical query.
  • Validate CDS extensibility, suitable data sources, association cardinality, and the final analytical results in the target system.
  • A separate custom report may not be necessary when the standard application is based on a suitably extensible CDS model.

Conclusion

This example demonstrates how an additional derived characteristic can be introduced into a standard CDS-based SAP Fiori analytical application when the available key-user extensibility options do not cover the requirement.

By extending the underlying Cube and analytical query, the Reporting Supplier was added without copying or replacing the standard Projects – Actuals application. This provides a useful option to evaluate before deciding to build a separate custom report.

References

  • SAP Help – Custom Fields and Logic
  • SAP Help – Creating Data Source Extensions
  • SAP Help – ABAP CDS: Extending CDS Views
  • SAP Help – Creating Custom Fields and Custom Business Logic
  • SAP Community – How to: Adding Product Hierarchy to Analytical CDS Views
  • SAP Community – Extending CDS Queries with CO-PA (WW) Fields
  • SAP Community – How to: Extension of CDS Views
  • SAP Community – Adding Field in Standard Fiori Apps of S/4HANA with Data Source Extensions
  • SAP Community – Custom Reusable Elements, Custom Business Objects and Data Source Extension to Add Fields in Standard VDM
  • SAP Community – How to: Extension of WebDynpro Configurations due to Changes in CDS Views

entry.title: FPM Team: Transport of BICS Bookmarks and SEARCH UIBB Views in the Cloud now available with 2608
entry.content:
Dear SAP Community,

In 2021, the Web Dynpro Multidimensional Data Grid App replaced the SAP Design Studio app as default reporting tool for drill-down reporting in SAP S/4HANA. This app is using the Search UIBB provided by FPM for variable selection.

For the two components 'Grid' and 'Search', used in the Web Dynpro Multidimensional Data Grid, it is possible to save the actual state in the actual system (search view for the variables and bookmark for the grid (layout for the grid and, if wanted, variables of the search)) . These bookmarks and saved searches are stored in the system locally and could originally not be transported automatically to other systems.

As described in the blog article  https://community.sap.com/t5/technology-blog-posts-by-sap/fpm-team-transport-of-bics-bookmarks-and-search-uibb-views/ba-p/13714317 transporting of public bookmarks and saved searches was possible for private cloud releases which have at least SAP_UI 7.57SP006 or SAP_BW 757 SP003. We from the FPM team, have now made it possible to transfer views and bookmarks from one system to another for public cloud. 

Now, with Public Cloud Edition 2608 we have enabled the transporting of public bookmarks and saved searches via ATO (Adaptation Transport Organizer). 

Any user is able to create public bookmarks and saved searches in the Webdynpro BICS Grid Applications and Public Saved searches in any FPM Application which uses the SEARCH UIBB.

App Export Software Collection

After creating these objects in the applications, you are able to add them to your software collection.
To do this, please open the tab CONTENT of your software collection in app 'Export Software Collection'. 
Via the button "Add Items" in the toolbar of the items table you can add these objects. 

Search for Type:

  • FPM_BKMK BICS Bookmarks
  • FPM_SEARCH Search Views

in the "Add Items" popup and select the items you want to transport. 

When checking and export your software collection, please make sure that the bookmarks are not locked by youtself in the running application. 

App Import Collection

After successfully exporting the software collection open the app 'Import Collection' in your target system and import the newly created objects there. 

If you change the transported object in the source system or even delete them you can transport these changes to your target system via these two apps accordingly.

If other users want to see the imported bookmarks and search views in there view list , please be aware of the new favorite concept.
After importing views/bookmarks the users will not automatically see the public entries. They have to add them manually to their list. This can be done in the Manage Dialog (Manage Views/ Manage Bookmarks ) and via settting these views as favorite. 

General Information on Import/Export Collection Apps

For more information on the transport scenario within the public cloud, see How to Manage and Export Your Software Collection, Export Collection and Import Collection.

 

Now you have learned how to transport saved searches and bookmarks from one system to another.

 

Please note that the transport of saved searches not only works for variable selection for the BICS Grid but for all Search configurations.

entry.title: Smarter Reporting with AI: Introducing the AI-Assisted Report Summary in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Ed
entry.content:
What's it about ?

If you have ever stared at a dense business report and wished it could explain itself? With the AI-Assisted KPI and Report Summary feature, that’s no longer wishful thinking—the insight you need is now built right into your SAP S/4HANA Cloud, public edition.

The AI-Assisted KPI and Report Summary feature, inside Smart Business reports created from the Manage KPIs and Reports app, uses SAP Business AI to generate natural-language summaries of your report data on demand. Whether you are a finance analyst reviewing spend patterns, a procurement manager checking supplier performance, or working with any type of complex datasets, this feature translates raw report data into readable, shareable text — without you having to manually interpret rows of figures.

Two Levels of Summary, One Click Away

The feature gives you two distinct summarization modes depending on the level of detail and granularity you need. You can choose between:

  • Report Summary — A comprehensive summary covering all measures and dimensions across every configured view in your report. When you want the full picture, choose this option.
  • View Summary — When you want to focus on a specific slice of data, choose this option to generate a focused summary scoped to one specific view within the report.

You can access both options through the Summarize button in the report menu — Summarize Report maps to Report Summary, and Summarize View maps to View Summary.

What You Can Do with a Generated Summary

Once the AI generates your summary, you are not limited to just reading it on screen. You can:

  • Review and analyze the data directly from the summary panel
  • Copy the content to your clipboard for use in emails, presentations, or documents
  • Share the summary via email directly from the app
  • Regenerate the summary for different views using the Refresh option
  • Regenerate the summary with drilldown or filters applied, to summarize the updated context of the report

How It Works

Here’s a quick demo of how this feature works:

video

Before You Get Started

This feature requires a few things to have in place.

First, you need to enable the AI-assisted KPI and Report Summary - Generate Summary option when creating a smart business report; it is not active by default. You can also enable AI-assisted Generate Summary for existing reports.

Your administrator also needs to assign the appropriate authorizations to your business role:

  • Business Catalog: Smart Business - AI Assisted KPI and Report Summary (SAP_CORE_BC_SSB_SUM_PC)
  • IAM App: AI-assisted KPI and Report Summary (F9188)

Because this is a Base AI feature, you’ll need to accept the Base AI–assisted features terms; see SAP Note 3651017 for details.

This feature is available from SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition 2608 onwards.

In short, the AI-Assisted KPI and Report Summary feature turns your reports into clear, shareable insights—right where you work in SAP S/4HANA Cloud, public edition. Enable it, verify the output, and let it accelerate your first-pass analysis, so you can focus on decisions that matter.

Have you tried it yet? Share your experience in the comments below.

A Note on AI-Generated Content

As with any AI-generated output, the summaries are a starting point, not a final word. SAP recommends independently verifying the information before using it for business decisions. Treat the summaries as an efficient first-pass analysis tool, not as a substitute for human judgment.

entry.title: Unlock Your KPI Insights Instantly with SAP Joule: Introducing the Smart Business KPI Capability
entry.content:
The Problem Every Business User Knows

Your company tracks dozens of KPIs. They're spread across finance, procurement, and operations — each living inside a different Fiori app, behind a different tile, reached through a different set of clicks. Every morning you navigate the same menus to find the same reports. The data is there. Getting to it is just... slow.

What if you could skip all of that and just ask?

Meet the Smart Business KPI Capability for SAP Joule

The Smart Business KPI (SSB KPI) Capability brings your performance dashboards directly into Joule's conversational interface. Ask a plain-language question — get a clickable, navigable KPI card back, right inside the chat pane.

No new configuration. No new data models. The Smart Business KPI capability connects directly to your existing setup.

See It in Action: An AR Manager's Morning

Take an Accounts Receivable Manager who needs to check Days Sales Outstanding (DSO) and related collection KPIs at the start of each day. Previously: open the Fiori Launchpad, locate the AR overview tile, navigate into the report.

Now they open Joule and type: "Show me my assigned KPIs."

Joule returns a KPI Overview card listing every Smart Business KPI assigned to their role — all 30-something of them. They spot the appropriate KPI immediately, click it, and land directly in the runtime report: live values, threshold indicators, trend charts. No manual effort or searching required, just a natural-language request and the relevant details, instantly ! This is the experience this capability is designed to deliver.

What You Can Ask

"Show me my assigned KPIs" · "List my KPIs" · "What KPIs do I have?"

Joule retrieves all Smart Business KPIs assigned to your user role — regardless of threshold status — and presents them in a KPI Overview card. Each item is a direct deep link: one click opens the KPI's runtime report in the correct Fiori application, with the evaluation context already applied.

Why It Matters

Zero navigation overhead

No need to remember which tile leads to which KPI. Just ask.

Role-relevant results only

You see exactly what you're assigned — nothing more, nothing less.

One click to live data

Every KPI card item deep-links to the runtime report with evaluation context pre-loaded.

Works in 40+ languages

Full localization including Arabic, Hebrew, Japanese, Chinese, and all major European languages.

Secure by design

Data retrieval uses your existing SSO session — users see only what they're already entitled to see.

No extra setup

Connects to your existing Smart Business KPI setup with no new data modeling required.

How It Works

When you ask Joule about your KPIs, it understands your intent, retrieves the relevant Smart Business KPIs using your existing SSO authentication, and formats them into a UI5 Integration Card native to the Joule interface.

Every item in the card carries Intent-Based Navigation (IBN) links — the KPI's Semantic Object, Action, and Evaluation or Report ID are embedded as parameters, so one click opens the exact right Fiori application with the exact right context.

Try it today: Ask Joule "Show me my assigned KPIs" in your SAP S/4HANA Cloud 2612 environment. We'd love to hear how it fits your workflow — share your experience in the comments.
